# Copilot instructions for this repository

This is the frontend for a tango-orchestra music guessing game: a client-only static
React + Vite PWA with no backend. Rounds present a 30-second preview clip; players guess
which orchestra performed it from 3 choices, with points based on how fast they answer
correctly.

## Important Override instructions
- Do not include any references to the parent repo or its specs in the generated code. This is a standalone
  repository and should not assume any knowledge of the parent repo.
- Do not include references to any other files outside of this repository. All code should be self-contained within this repository.


## Commands

Run everything from this directory (`frontend/`, the repo root).

```bash
npm install
npm run dev              # Vite dev server at :5173
npm run build             # tsc -b && vite build -> dist/
npm run preview           # serve the production build locally
npm run build:catalogue   # regenerate public/catalogue/starter-catalogue.json from tools/build-catalogue/archive-org-tracks.ts
npm run build:sounds      # regenerate public/sounds/correct.wav and incorrect.wav
```

Tests:

```bash
npm run test:unit        # vitest run tests/unit
npm run test:component   # vitest run tests/component
npm run test:coverage    # full vitest run with coverage (this is what `npm test` and CI run)
npm run test:e2e         # playwright (desktop + mobile projects), auto-starts the dev server
```

To run a single test file or case, invoke vitest/playwright directly rather than through the
npm scripts, e.g.:

```bash
npx vitest run tests/unit/scoring.test.ts
npx vitest run tests/unit/scoring.test.ts -t "scores track 1"
npx playwright test tests/e2e/smoke.spec.ts --project=desktop
```

There is no lint script configured; rely on `tsc -b` (part of `npm run build`) for type
checking.

**Coverage gate** (`vitest.config.ts`): 80% lines/functions/statements/branches overall.
`src/telemetry/**`, `src/main.tsx`, and config files are excluded from coverage. The pure
game engine (`src/game/engine/**`) is expected to stay near 100% — check `npm run
test:coverage` output per-file, not just the aggregate.

Playwright is configured with a hardcoded `executablePath: '/usr/bin/chromium-browser'`
(`playwright.config.ts`) — e2e tests will fail on machines where Chromium isn't at that path.

## Architecture

**Data flow**: `App.tsx` is the only stateful component; it owns `catalogue`, `session`,
`elapsedMs`, countdown/preparation lifecycle state, plus track, countdown, and feedback audio-player refs, and renders one of the screen components in
`src/ui/screens/` based on derived state (no router — `src/app/routes.ts` only defines a
`Screen` union type that isn't currently wired to a router). There is no
reducer/context — state transitions all happen inline in `App.tsx` by calling
`reduceSession` and updating `useState`.

**Game engine is pure and framework-free** (`src/game/engine/`): `session.ts`
(`createSession`/`reduceSession`), `selection.ts` (round/orchestra/track randomisation),
`scoring.ts` (`scoreCorrect`, a linear decay from a per-track-number max to min score over
0–30s, plus flat `WRONG_GUESS_POINTS`/`SKIP_POINTS`). `reduceSession` is a pure
event-reducer: given a `Session` and a `SessionEvent` (`GUESS_CORRECT` / `GUESS_WRONG` /
`SKIP` / `TRACK_ENDED` / `NEXT_ROUND`), it returns a new `Session` via `structuredClone` +
mutation of the clone — never mutates the input. This is why the engine hits ~100% coverage
and is tested independently of React (`tests/unit/`).

**Session/Round/Track shape** (`src/game/types.ts`): a `Session` has exactly 3 `Round`s
(indices `0|1|2`); each `Round` has a `correctOrchestraId`, 3 `choiceOrchestraIds`
(multiple-choice options), up to 3 `trackIds`, and one `TrackAttempt` per track
(`trackNumber: 1|2|3`). A round is `won` on first correct guess, `exhausted` once all 3
attempts are used without a correct guess. The session is `complete` once round index 2
resolves.

**Catalogue is a separately-loaded JSON asset, not bundled code**
(`src/game/catalogue/catalogue.ts`): `loadCatalogue()` fetches
`{BASE_URL}catalogue/starter-catalogue.json` at runtime and validates it with
`validateCatalogue` (exactly 5 orchestras matching `ORCHESTRA_IDS`, unique track IDs, every
track's `previewUrl` must be `https://` **unless** `catalogue.version` starts with
`test-catalogue-` and the URL starts with `/audio/` — a special-cased local-only escape
hatch). Two catalogue files exist:
- `public/catalogue/starter-catalogue.json` — the real, committed production catalogue:
  15 archive.org-hosted MP3 tracks (3 per orchestra), generated by
  `npm run build:catalogue` from the source list in
  `tools/build-catalogue/archive-org-tracks.ts`. Edit that source list, not the JSON
  directly, then regenerate.
- `public/catalogue/test-catalogue.json` — local-only synthetic speech clips
  (`public/audio/*.wav`), each announcing its orchestra/track number. **`vite.config.ts`
  has a dev-only server middleware** that transparently serves this file's contents in
  place of `starter-catalogue.json` whenever `npm run dev` is running — `npm run
  build`/`preview`/production always serve the real committed `starter-catalogue.json`
  file as-is. Automated tests bypass both by importing/mocking the JSON fixture directly.

**Audio playback** (`src/game/audio/player.ts`): a thin wrapper around a single shared
`HTMLAudioElement`, exposing `prepare`/`playPrepared` for pre-round loading and
`play`/`stop`/`getElapsedMs`/`onEnded`/`onError` for normal playback. Preparation sets the
source and waits for media readiness without starting playback, so elapsed scoring remains
at zero until the countdown completes. `App.tsx`
polls `getElapsedMs()` on a 100ms interval while a round is active to drive the "score
ticking down" display and to timestamp `GUESS_CORRECT` events — elapsed time from this
poll, not the engine's own clock, is what `scoreCorrect` scores against.

**Answer feedback audio** (`src/game/audio/feedback-sound-player.ts`) is deliberately
separate from track playback. It uses the Web Audio API and cached decoded buffers for the
short correct/incorrect cues under `public/sounds/`; this avoids affecting the existing
`HTMLMediaElement` playback call-count assertions in component tests. Playback failures are
non-fatal and must never interrupt gameplay.

**Round countdown** (`src/ui/screens/CountdownScreen.tsx`) is presentational only. `App.tsx`
owns the 5-to-1 timers, starts first-track preparation at 5, and uses a monotonically
increasing preparation ID to prevent abandoned or superseded countdowns from starting stale
audio. After the final pip, a one-second pause keeps the final count visible before the round and
track start. `src/game/audio/countdown-sound-player.ts` uses a separate Web Audio context
for the five short pips and final longer pip. Component tests should use short injected
`countdownStepMs`/`countdownEndPauseMs` values or fake timers and must cover cue counts,
preparation ordering, delayed readiness, failures, and stale-work cancellation.

**GitHub Pages base path**: `vite.config.ts`'s `base` reads `process.env.GITHUB_PAGES_BASE`
(set only by `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` to `/<repo-name>/` for project-site
builds); `loadCatalogue` reads `import.meta.env.BASE_URL` rather than a hardcoded `/` so both
locally-served and Pages-subpath-served builds resolve the catalogue fetch correctly.

## Conventions

- **`.npmrc` pins `registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/`** for this project specifically —
  don't remove this. It exists because some environments' global npm config points at an
  internal-only registry; without this override, `package-lock.json` would bake in internal
  URLs that CI/GitHub Actions can't resolve.
- Business-logic modules (`src/game/**`) have no React/DOM imports and are tested in
  `tests/unit/`; anything importing React or touching the DOM is tested in
  `tests/component/` with React Testing Library + jsdom.
- Session/round/attempt objects are treated as immutable at the API boundary
  (`reduceSession` clones before mutating) even though the engine isn't written with a
  formal immutability library — follow this pattern for any new engine functions.
- Orchestra IDs are a closed, ordered union (`ORCHESTRA_IDS` in `src/game/types.ts`); the
  game is intentionally limited to these five (Carlos Di Sarli, Juan D'Arienzo, Anibal
  Troilo, Osvaldo Pugliese, Astor Piazzolla).
